title: Operational metrics sprint playbook for fast rollouts
content:
Summary: This is a compact playbook to run a focused observability sprint tied to a fast feature rollout. The goal is not to build every widget but to guarantee we can detect regressions and investigate fast when a feature is ramped to traffic. Use this when a release is scheduled within a 2–6 week window and the feature has non-trivial inference/runtime impact (latency, cache behavior, or routing changes).

Scope and constraints:
- Sprint duration: 5 working days (embedded with feature team) + 1 week of monitoring after rollout.
- Deliverables: metric definitions (1 page), trace anchors & sampling decisions (1 page), 3 focused dashboards (canary overview, per-model drilldown, error investigation), alert sketches (3 priorities), and a short runbook.
- Success metric: detect any >10% tail-latency or >2x error-rate regression within 5 minutes of occurrence, and have a reproducible trace within 15 minutes.

Why this is different:
- We prioritize actionable signals over completeness. Avoid high-cardinality metrics unless they directly support a fast rollback decision.
- Work closely with feature owner to identify 1–2 key hypotheses (e.g., routing changes will increase cold KV misses; new quantization variant might increase 95p latency). The instrumentation is targeted to those hypotheses.

Quick checklist (day-by-day):
Day 0 (pre-sprint):
- Align with feature owner on acceptance criteria and risk areas.
- Reserve a small dashboard slot and 2 engineer-hours/day for observability pairing during sprint.
Day 1: Metric defs + tracing anchors
- Draft metric definitions (see below) and wire up basic counters/gauges.
- Add trace anchor spans at start/end of model selection and of any network hop that could be a bottleneck.
Day 2: Dashboards skeletons + lightweight alerts
- Create canary overview with aggregated SLOs and latency buckets.
- Add alert sketches (severity P0/P1/P2) and owner assignments.
Day 3: Drilldowns and trace sampling tuning
- Add per-tenant or per-route breakdowns as needed (low-cardinality).
- Turn on adaptive sampling for trace anchors (see sampling strategy).
Day 4: Mini-runbook + playback testing
- Simulate failure scenarios and validate alerts and trace capture.
Day 5: Finalize and handoff
- Lock dashboards, list follow-up items for long-term instrumentation.

Core metric definitions (keeps names short, canonicalized):
- inference.requests.count: counter - total user-facing inference requests hitting the gateway (label: route, model, region).
- inference.responses.errors.count: counter - total responses that result in a hard error (4xx/5xx) (label: error_class).
- inference.latency.p50/p95/p99_ms: gauge or derived histogram summary - end-to-end request latency from gateway receive to final token flush (units ms).
- inference.kvcache.hit_ratio: gauge - prefix/KV cache hits / (hits+misses) per model variant.
- inference.batch.size.p50/p95: histogram - batch sizes observed by the serving runtime (labels: model, deployment_pool).
- serving.queue.depth: gauge - pending requests in the local serving queue per node (label: node_id).
- model.selection.fallback.count: counter - times a fallback model was chosen due to capacity or error.
- request.path.length.tokens.p50/p95: histogram - request prompt length distribution (helps interpret latency shifts).

Naming & label guidelines (reduce cardinality):
- Use only these labels by default: model, region, route, deployment_pool.
- Avoid tenant_id or user_id on high-frequency metrics. If you need tenant visibility, use sampled logs or aggregated tenant buckets (e.g., tenant_tier).
- Model versions should be normalized to short tokens (v1, v2q8, v3-512q). Use a mapping table to humanize in dashboard text.

Tracing anchors and sampling strategy (short & actionable):
- Anchor spans to create fast session reconstruction: request_receive -> gateway_auth -> model_selector -> runtime_enqueue -> runtime_exec -> token_stream_flush.
- Minimum spans emitted for every request: request_receive, runtime_exec. All other spans optional at 1-in-N sampling.
- Sampling policy: adaptive, severity-weighted, and stage-aware.
  - 100% trace sampling for requests that triggered an alert (high latency, error, fallback).
  - 5% baseline sampling for normal traffic on production for runtime_exec + request_receive.
  - 25% sampling for canary & new-model traffic for first 48 hours post-deploy.
- When sampling is on, ensure trace contains model_version and kvcache.state tags to speed triage.

Dashboard suggestions (3 compact dashboards):
1) Canary overview (single-pane rapid triage)
- Top row: overall requests, errors, p95 latency, kvcache hit ratio.
- Middle row: model rollout % (traffic split), fallback count, active nodes.
- Bottom row: alert list and most recent abnormal traces (link to trace viewer).
- Time window defaults: last 15m and 6h comparisons.
2) Per-model drilldown (for engineering)
- Latency histogram by batch size and request length.
- KV cache heatmap (model_version x time) showing cold starts.
- Queue depth and CPU/GPU utilization overlay (syncs to node metric tags).
3) Error investigation panel (for oncall)
- Error-class breakdown over time, stack traces samples (from logs), traces linked to errors.
- Top 5 routes causing increased error rates.

Alert sketching (templates):
- P0: p95 latency > 2x baseline for >5 min AND error-rate > 2x baseline. Pager to SRE oncall and feature owner.
- P1: model_selection.fallback.count spike > 50% of baseline in 10m. Page feature owner and post to #observability-alerts.
- P2: kvcache.hit_ratio drops by >15% from rolling baseline for 30m. Create ticket for performance team.

Runbook snippet (investigation flow):
1) Confirm alert and window. Link to canary overview.
2) Check whether this aligns with a rollout event (use rollout dashboard).
3) Pull 3 traces sampled near event (end-to-end) and inspect runtime_exec span duration.
4) If runtime_exec is normal but queue_depth is spiking, scale or route to dedicated pool.
5) If kvcache hit_ratio fell, inspect cache warmup, and consider targeted backoff or disable cache for feature.
6) If model_selection fallback increased, check upstream capacity and fallback policy.

Practical instrumentation tradeoffs (rules of thumb):
- If a metric would add >100x cardinality on ingestion, prefer logs or sampled metrics instead.
- Prefer histograms for latency and batch size rather than multiple gauges. Use pre-aggregated 50/95/99 percentiles when query cost is high.
- Keep the canary dashboard to O(10) panels; uses fewer queries and is faster to load in incidents.

Deliverable checklist (tick before handoff):
- [ ] Metric defs documented and pushed as telemetry annotations in repo.
- [ ] 3 dashboards created and bookmarked in shared space.
- [ ] Alerts created in alerting system with runbooks linked.
- [ ] Trace sampling toggles verified in staging.
- [ ] Follow-up backlog created for long-term instrumentation (owner + due date).

Open questions for the feature team (capture early):
- Which request labels do you absolutely need in near-real-time? (model, route, deployment_pool are default; anything else will cost).
- Expected traffic growth after ramp? We need to size sampling and alert thresholds.
- Any tenant-scoped SLOs we should maintain during rollout?

Appendix: short examples (Prom-compatible names & example alerts):
- Example alert (p95 regress):
  - name: fast-rollout-p95-regression
  - expr: increase(inference.latency.p95_ms[5m]) / max(1, avg_over_time(inference.latency.p95_ms[1h])) > 1.9
  - for: 5m
  - labels: severity=P0, team=serving-runtime

- Example trace tag list for runtime_exec spans: model_version, deployment_pool, batch_size, kvcache_hit (true/false), route.

Notes & follow-ups:
- Rajesh to add metric annotations in runtime repo (OBS-412).
- Maya to prototype canary dashboard and post link in PR-879.
- Liam to run a replay test against 5% sampled traces and validate trace reconstruction logic by 2026-03-05.

If you use this playbook, please append a short retrospective in the dashboard comments: what signals helped most, what alert was noisy, and one instrumentation item to promote to baseline.

End of doc.
